summary: This article explains how a star forms from a cloud of gas and dust, shines for millions of years through nuclear fusion, and reaches a different end depending on its size.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “How Stars Are Born and Die” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: a light gas that is the main fuel stars use to shine
to fall inward or cave in suddenly

challengeTerms.def: existing or happening between the stars
to start burning or to begin suddenly and powerfully
to use up a supply of something until little or none is left

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that learning how a star is born is more interesting than learning how a star dies? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Describe, in order, the main stages of a star's life from a cloud of gas to its final end.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review hydrogen, collapse, and core, and let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use interstellar, ignite, and deplete in a short paragraph that compares two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
